thread:
alex: Heads-up — since ~08:20 UTC we're seeing a lot of gRPC streaming token stalls from the us-west-2 GPU fleet. p95 token latency jumped from ~80ms to ~600ms, and rpc deadline misses spiked. Any ideas?

maya: Seeing the same. Canary pool nodes in az-b are worst. p99 token stream tail ~2.3s. Dropped streams + some resetting streams.

sam: Quick check — are we seeing TCP-level retransmits/reordering on the NICs? I/O and GPU queues look fine.

maya: tcpdump from one host shows weird sequence ordering — packets arriving out of sequence in bursts. here's a short pcap dump I grabbed:```
18:20:05.001234 IP 10.10.12.5.443 > 10.10.34.12.57032: Flags [P.], seq 100000:100444, ack 200001, win 4096, length 444
18:20:05.001256 IP 10.10.12.5.443 > 10.10.34.12.57032: Flags [P.], seq 100888:101332, ack 200001, win 4096, length 444
18:20:05.001280 IP 10.10.12.5.443 > 10.10.34.12.57032: Flags [P.], seq 100444:100888, ack 200001, win 4096, length 444
```
That's out-of-order bursts (100888 arrived before 100444).

zhang: That pattern smells like NIC offload reordering or a RoCE/driver issue on the path between ToR and host. Any recent firmware/driver rollouts?

alex: We rolled an ixgbe/ena driver update to a subset of nodes last night (kernel module v5.10.12 -> v5.11.0). Targeted for perf improvements.

sam: Can you paste ethtool stats for an affected NIC? look for rx_missed_errors, rx_no_desc, rx_oom, or any reorder counters. Also check RDMA counters if RoCE is enabled.

maya: ethtool -S output (trimmed):```
ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "reorder|rx_|tx_"
rx_packets: 123456789
rx_errors: 0
rx_missed: 3
rx_short: 0
flow_reordered_count: 412
```
We do have a non-zero flow_reordered_count. RDMA link show:```
rdma link show
mlx5_0 port 1: up (RDMA over Converged Ethernet)
link_speed: 100Gbps
retrans_error: 0
rcv_seq_err: 56
```

sam: rcv_seq_err=56 is concerning. That matches the tcpdump. Which switches/ToRs are these hosts connected to?

alex: az-b ToR is Broadcom-based 7320s; az-a is mostly Mellanox. The affected hosts are on 7320s, the ones with driver rollouts are also on az-b.

zhang: Broadcom + certain NIC offloads can re-order under heavy bursty queues if combined with GRO/LRO and switch-level rebalancing. Try disabling GRO/LRO on one host as a quick canary:```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off
```
If that drops reordering counters we know offload is the culprit.

maya: Doing that on one node now. Also increasing grpc deadline temporarily to reduce app impact (1s -> 2s) and cordoning that node from GPU pool.

infra-bot: [alert] 2 instances cordoned in us-west-2/az-b by maya. Incident ticket #INC-2026-314 opened.

sam: Also check switch ASIC counters for rebalancing/ECMP churn and any recent config pushes. If ToR is doing flow steering across spines differently after config, it could flip packet order. Can we get a switch pkt capture for the flow?

alex: I pulled a 10-second pcap at the ToR for that flow; sending to infra-dropbox.

maya: Quick test results: after disabling GRO/GSO on the host, flow_reordered_count stopped increasing and token stream latency dropped back to ~120ms on that host. Other affected hosts still show spikes.

zhang: That strongly implicates host-side offloads interacting poorly with the path. Two mitigations: 1) roll back the driver update on the subset we pushed, or 2) disable GRO/LRO/GSO globally until vendor patch. Driver rollback is quicker for a small set.

sam: Agree. Rollback plan: revert driver on the 6 nodes we updated in az-b, monitor reorder counters for 30m, if stable we can schedule broader rollback or vendor escalation. Also collect full pcap and firmware/driver versions for vendor.

alex: Rolling back driver on the canary nodes now. Scheduling a broader block if metrics improve.

sre-oncall: Noted. Also flagging customer-facing latency alerts and updated status page. Keep me posted before doing mass changes.

maya: After rollback on the first two nodes: reorder counters steady, p95 tokens back to baseline. Opening vendor support case with Broadcom + NIC vendor including pcaps + ethtool -S dumps + rdma counters.

zhang: Long-term: we should add an automated check in infra-exporter for flow_reordered_count/rcv_seq_err and a canary post-driver-rollout smoke test (disable offloads + quick token stream).

alex: Agreed. Action items: 1) finish rollback for the remaining updated nodes in az-b (sam/maya), 2) vendor ticket with artifacts (maya), 3) add exporter metric + rollout smoke test (zhang), 4) keep RPC deadline bump until fleet stable (alex).

infra-bot: [incident] INC-2026-314 status -> triaged; priority P2; assignees: maya, sam, zhang.

maya: I'll update the incident with the pcap link and timeline. markers: driver roll -> spike -> disable offload -> rollback -> improvement.

alex: Thanks team. If rollback doesn't hold we'll consider disabling offloads fleet-wide and emergency firmware rollback. For now, monitoring. :thumbsup:
